title: What'a ahead for markets, AI as 'blue wave' sweeps Congress
excerpt: Markets rallied on Wednesday after Democrats surged in the midterms. Market pros see implications for the AI trade and broader fiscal issues.
content_html:
What investing pros see ahead for markets after the Democrats win Congress

By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

The seismic shift in the political landscape after Tuesday's midterms is still being assessed, but investing pros are starting to get a handle on what it might mean for markets.

The Democrats' sweep puts them back in control of both the Senate and House. While that's a momentous political development, given the now-divided government, it's also a recipe for gridlock. That tends to be a positive scenario for markets, which are often anxious about the prospect of sweeping change to things like policy or regulation.

Data center fight takes center stage

The AI trade is a possible wrinkle in the outlook, though, particularly the data center buildout.

"On AI and data center regulation, Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to have significant implications," wrote Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius on Wednesday. "The states where Democrats are likely to further restrict data centers account for roughly 45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas alone accounting for roughly 25%."

Morgan Stanley previously highlighted several states with data center projects that could be compromised by a political flip, almost all of which were won by democrats on Tuesday.

Texas flipped a Senate seat and a governorship blue on Tuesday, as well as a handful of other state positions and four state supreme court seats. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has been a more staunch opponent of data centers than Greg Abbott, whose moratorium on development was expected to soften after the election in the event that he won.

"State and local rules remain more important for data center timing and location," wrote Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, CIO of UBS Americas. "The composition of state governments, including the result in Texas, may prove more consequential for individual data center projects than the change in congressional control."

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives, a tech and AI mega-bull addressed the midterms in a note to investors, saying that it will likely pose considerable hurdles for the AI expansion over the next two years.

"The biggest worry of the night for tech investors and the AI trade was around the state of Texas where ~25%-30% of data center gigawatts and capacity will come from…with Democrat Gina Hinojosa winning the Texas Governor race in a surprise over incumbent Greg Abbott," Ives wrote.

A shifting fiscal outlook

George Saravelos, global head of FX Research at Deutsche Bank, said that the debt ceiling is now a major item on the agenda heading into next year, noting that the Republicans could raise the debt limit via reconciliation in the coming weeks.

"If this succeeds, it will remove one additional layer of uncertainty on fiscal policy, while also preventing AI and other policy matters from getting bundled up in a protracted negotiation with a Democratic Congress," he said.

With Democrats' victory has also come recalibrated expectations for the US fiscal situation. If Democrats curtail Trump's ability to go to war when they take power, the outlook for the deficit could improve. Trump's statement ahead of the vote indicating he had no plans to resume strikes on Iran also sent oil prices tumbling, pushing bond yields down as investors adjusted expectations for inflation and interest rates.

Other finance pros urged investors not to panic about the election's knock-on effects on things like AI. Mark Malek, CIO of Siebert Financial said that although the market impacts of the blue wave are real, the AI-led bull market won't be derailed.

He added that although data center costs could rise, the cost of AI buildout hasn't stopped Big Tech hyperscalers, who are still committed to spending huge sums on more infrastructure in 2027 and beyond.

"Every tax break that disappears and every megawatt a builder has to generate for itself comes straight out of the return on that capital," he stated. "For investors, that is not a reason to run from the AI trade. It is a reason to read the margin line a little more carefully when the next round of earnings comes in."

塞缪尔·奥布莱恩 (Samuel O'Brient) 是一位经验丰富的金融市场和商业记者，撰写的文章涉及经济、技术和公共政策等广泛主题。 在《商业内幕》中，他报道了重要的宏观和微观经济故事，包括顶尖经济学家和对冲基金经理的观点、首次公开募股失败、企业破产、迷因股票和卖空。 他还撰写有关加密货币、石油和房地产等其他市场的文章。他采访了许多市场上最有影响力的声音，从马克·赞迪和理查德·塞勒等顶级经济学家到丹尼·摩西、安德鲁·莱夫特、安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇、路易斯·纳维利尔和格兰特·卡登等著名投资者。福克斯的 LiveNOW、Taking Stock 和 Ticker News 等节目让塞缪尔讨论股市和经济发展。 他的报道曾被纽约时报 DealBook、彭博电台、福布斯、Entrepreneur、Gizmodo 和 TheFutureParty 引用。Samuel 最初在 InvestorPlace 工作，报道投资、零售交易和宏观经济趋势。 在加入 Business Insider 之前，他曾担任 TheStreet 的技术市场记者。 他毕业于莎拉·劳伦斯学院和都柏林三一学院。Samuel 的作品曾发表在 TipRanks、EV 和 Observer 等出版物上。 当他不追寻故事时，人们经常会发现他在逛书店和唱片店。 要联系 Samuel，请发送电子邮件至 sobrient@insider.com 或通过 LinkedIn 与他联系。 他还在《信号》中饰演塞缪尔·克莱门斯。
